QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_13

question.text: Anil's equity fund delivered 18% return with a standard deviation of 12%. A debt fund delivered 9% return with a standard deviation of 3%. Risk-free rate is 6%. Which fund has a better Sharpe Ratio?

answer.text: Equity fund with Sharpe Ratio of 1.50
Debt fund with Sharpe Ratio of 1.50
Both have equal Sharpe Ratios of 1.00
Equity fund with Sharpe Ratio of 2.00

explanation.text: The Logic: Sharpe Ratio = (Return - Risk-free rate) / Standard deviation. Equity fund: (18% - 6%) / 12% = 1.00. Debt fund: (9% - 6%) / 3% = 1.00. Both schemes deliver equal return per unit of risk, so neither is preferable on Sharpe alone. The Trap: Options A and D wrongly assign a Sharpe of 1.50 or 2.00 to the equity fund (arithmetic error). Option B wrongly assigns a Sharpe of 1.50 to the debt fund. The Sharpe formula equalises the two funds at 1.00. Note: Distributor coaching prose removed; explanation rewritten with the source Sharpe calculation and the equal-return-per-unit-of-risk interpretation.
